doc.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Researching the guitar book: Charlie Christian to roots
summary: She plans to start with Charlie Christian, Wes Montgomery and George Benson, and dig into early blues and New Orleans guitar, with Freddie Green mentioned.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: So when you go to approach a book, okay now I’m going to write about guitarists, how do you start something like that? Do you start doing your own research and look into what’s available to listen to, or do you visit an archive?

Well, yeah, I’m going to do all that. But I know I’m going to begin with Charlie Christian, and I’m going to go from Charlie Christian on to Wes Montgomery, and there are others, Eddie Lang and Oscar Moore in the older crowd. So I mean by now there’s a certain amount I’ve picked up enough to know who were the major influences, who were the major stylists, and who I’ll concentrate on and who comes from them and who listened to them. And then on to George Benson. And so I have some ideas. But I’m going to go and look at the books that have already been written for adults, and I’m going to go back and listen to a lot of music, and I’m going to go and try to see what I can find about among the New Orleans guitarists, because I’m not aware of any really, and I’m sure there are some — oh of course, what am I talking about — Danny Barker the banjo player, but he was a banjo player. But maybe that’s where, you know I have to go back to the roots and find out about the roots of jazz guitar, because I guess it’s — yeah, what’s his name, cousin Joseph, cousin Joe. I think he started on guitar and then he had to play piano one night when his piano player didn’t show up and so he went over to playing the piano, but he plays guitar. I guess those early blues players all did.
So many people that we’ve talked to have always mentioned Freddie Green too. Even though he wasn’t a major soloist, he set the —

But he’s later on. I’m talking about before. I’ll go to Freddie Green, that was a big name. And he gave Basie’s rhythm section a special sound. Very important. But I’m going to go back to the roots and see who were the first. Because all of the blues players played guitar. That’s where that came from.
